body:
## Summary

`formal-ai with <tool> …` builds the native CLI's argv incorrectly in five distinct ways. All five
are reproducible on **formal-ai 0.317.0** with a fake CLI first on `PATH` that records its argv.
They are grouped here because they share one cause — argv is assembled by string surgery over the
caller's flags rather than by parsing them — but each can be fixed and tested independently.

## Reproduction

Script: [`repro-with-argv.sh`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/experiments/issue-2130/repro-with-argv.sh) ·
stored output: [`wrapper-argv.log`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-2130/data/runs/wrapper-argv.log)

It puts a shim that prints `argv` and the stdin byte count first on `PATH`, then invokes each tool in
the two shapes a caller realistically uses:

```bash
# A — prompt as an argument
formal-ai with <tool> --model formal-ai -p "<prompt>" --verbose
# B — prompt piped
echo "<prompt>" | formal-ai with <tool> --model formalai/formal-ai --verbose
```

---

### 1. The provider prefix is applied twice for `agent`

Shape B, caller passes `--model formalai/formal-ai`:

```text
agent --no-summarize-session --compaction-model same --model formalai/formalai/formal-ai --interactive
```

`formalai/` is prepended unconditionally instead of only when the selector is unqualified. An
already-qualified selector should be passed through unchanged.

### 2. `--verbose` is silently dropped for every tool

In shape B no tool receives `--verbose` — not `agent`, `gemini`, `qwen`, `claude` or `codex`. A flag
the caller explicitly asked for should either be forwarded or rejected with a message, never dropped
silently. This one is self-aggravating: it removes exactly the output needed to notice the other four.

### 3. `--interactive` is injected into a piped, headless invocation

Shape B gives `agent` an `--interactive` flag the caller never asked for, while stdin is a pipe. In
hive-mind#2130 this made the run enter `"mode": "stdin-stream"` with `alwaysAcceptStdin: true` and
never terminate on its own; the harness stopped it at its 5/5 auto-restart limit. When stdin is not a
TTY, interactive mode should not be selected.

### 4. `codex` is given flags `codex exec` does not have, and loses `exec` when piped

Shape A:

```text
codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox workspace-write -c … --json -p <prompt> --verbose
```

`codex exec` has **no `-p` flag**, so this cannot parse.

Shape B is worse — the `exec` subcommand is missing entirely:

```text
codex --sandbox read-only -c model_providers.formalai.… -c model="formalai/formal-ai"
```

so codex launches its interactive TUI instead of running a non-interactive turn. codex takes its
prompt as a positional argument to `exec`, or on stdin; `-p` is a claude/agent/qwen spelling and
should not be forwarded to codex at all.

### 5. Caller passthrough flags do not survive a retry

Attempt 1 for `claude` forwards the caller's flags (and duplicates two of them —
`--output-format stream-json` and `--verbose` each appear twice, once from the wrapper and once from
the caller). But when the workspace-effect check fails, attempt 2 rebuilds argv from scratch:

```text
claude --model formal-ai --permission-mode acceptEdits --output-format stream-json --verbose --print <recovery prompt>
```

`--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--strict-mcp-config`, `--mcp-config <path>` and the entire
`--disallowedTools` list are **gone**. The retry therefore runs with a different permission posture
and a different toolset than the attempt the caller configured. For a headless caller, losing
`--dangerously-skip-permissions` is the difference between a run that completes and one that blocks
on a prompt nobody will answer.

Note the ladder only engages for prompts classified as coding tasks; a trivial prompt runs once, which
is why this needs a coding-task prompt to reproduce.

## Suggested fix

The common fix is to parse the caller's argv into a structured record — prompt, model, and a
per-tool-normalised set of options — and re-render it per tool, rather than concatenating strings.
Concretely:

- Treat the model selector as `provider/model` and only prepend `formalai/` when no provider is
  present (fixes 1).
- Keep the caller's flags in the record so retries re-render the *same* option set with only the
  prompt substituted (fixes 5, and removes the duplication).
- Give each client a declared flag vocabulary — codex has `exec`, no `-p`, and takes its prompt
  positionally; claude has `--print` and `-p` — and render through it (fixes 4).
- Forward unknown-but-explicit flags such as `--verbose` rather than dropping them, or fail loudly
  (fixes 2).
- Select interactive mode from `isatty(stdin)`, not unconditionally (fixes 3).

Regression tests are cheap here and would have caught all five: run each client with a shim on `PATH`
and assert on the exact argv.

## Related

- Downstream: link-assistant/hive-mind#2130
- Provider-block loss for codex: #902
- Full analysis: [case study §3.1.1 and §3.2.1](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-2130/README.md)

comments.body:
Correction to defect 3 in the report above, from my own follow-up testing.

I wrote that the injected `--interactive` made the run "never terminate on its own; the harness
stopped it at its 5/5 auto-restart limit." **The termination half of that claim is wrong**, and I
want it on the record before anyone spends time on it.

I drove `agent` 0.25.5 — the version from the production logs — against a live
`formal-ai serve --agent-mode`, with stdin a pipe closed immediately after the prompt, with and
without the flag:

```
agent 0.25.5
piped stdin, closed immediately after the prompt:
  args as the caller sends them             exit=0  4s  exited on its own
  + --interactive (what the wrapper injects) exit=0  4s  exited on its own
```

Both shapes exit cleanly. `agent` handles closed piped stdin correctly in interactive mode; it does
not hang. The restart loop I attributed to it was the calling harness's own
auto-restart-until-mergeable feature (`Max restart iterations: 5`) reacting to a run that produced no
work product — a consequence of the argv defects, not of a stuck process.

Defect 3 itself stands: shape B still adds `--interactive` to a headless, piped invocation the caller
never asked for, and the run still records `"mode": "stdin-stream"` / `alwaysAcceptStdin: true`.
Selecting interactive mode from `isatty(stdin)` is still the right fix. Only the severity is lower
than I first stated — it is a correctness bug in argv construction, not a hang.

Defects 1, 2, 4 and 5 are unaffected.

title: `formal-ai with <tool>` builds the native CLI's argv incorrectly: doubled provider prefix, dropped `--verbose`, injected `--interactive`, unsupported `-p` for codex, and caller flags lost on retry
